content:
After months of drama, Marvel's DNX crossover has come to an end. This major X-Men/Fantastic Four crossover wraps as we knew it would, with one last showdown between Cyclops and the Chairman, the fallen Hank McCoy. And by the time the dust of this battle settles, the X-Men are faced with a major tragedy and an arguably even bigger problem ahead.

Read on for a full breakdown of what happens in the DNX finale, but beware of spoilers for DNX #5!

Cyclops and Beast's Final Battle

At its core, DNX is an ideological conflict between Cyclops and his former friend, Beast. Both mutants saw a future where mutants dominate the planet in the Age of Revelation crossover. Cyclops seeks to prevent that future, while the Chairman (which has become the de facto name of this version of Beast to distinguish him from the younger, cloned version who still serves with the X-Men) wants to bring it to pass by any means necessary.

In recent issues, the Chairman nearly succeeded in detonating a bomb to transform the residents of Juniper, PA, into mutants, but the bomb was only partly successful. The mutants in question were deformed and barely clinging to life. The Chairman now hopes to destroy the town and try again elsewhere, while Cyclops seeks to save these poor, tortured souls and stop his old friend for good.

The two mutants battle it out amid the ruins of Juniper, with the Chairman lashing out because he feels that the X-Men abandoned him when they should have helped him save mutantkind from extinction. Cyclops manages to stab out one of the Chairman's eyes and incapacitate him, and he then sets about disarming the villain's bomb. But the Chairman attacks him again before Cyclops can finish deactivating the bomb's batteries.

As the fight continues, Cyclops finally seems to break through to his old friend and make Beast understand he's been wrong. But it's too late for either of them. Ultimately, the bomb detonates with one battery left attached, which creates an explosion just large enough to vaporize both Cyclops and the Chairman. Juniper has been saved, but at the cost of the life of the X-Men's intrepid leader.

The Return of the Phoenix

The X-Men have little time to mourn the death of their leader and the corrupted version of Beast before it becomes clear that they have another problem on their hands. Cyclops shares a psionic bond with Jean Grey, who's been busy out in space in the couple of years since the end of the Krakoan Age. Jean immediately feels her husband's death, and to say she's upset about this development would be a major understatement.

Jean seems finally ready to return home, and she's not at all happy. Every other time the Phoenix has made a beeline for Earth, there's been major trouble. Wll this time be any different? Will Jean become overwhelmed in her vulnerable state and lose control of her immense power?

Based on solicitations for future issues of writer Jed MacKay's X-Men series, it looks like Jean will stay planetside and replace Cyclops as the team leader going forward. She'll also be starring in a new Jean Grey solo series, and we know Marvel has a brand-new X-Men comic ready to go called Maximum X-Men. In short, the X-Men are going to keep very busy even as they mourn Cyclops.

DNX's Post-Credits Scene

As is tradition these days, DNX #5 ends with a "post-credits scene" that offers one last tease for the future. It turns out that Cyclops and the Chairman aren't dead after all. Both mutants emerge in a secret laboratory, where Beast tells Cyclops, "You've slept long enough. I am only now realizing that we both have."

It seems that Beast managed to teleport them both to safety as the bomb detonated. But for some reason, he's keeping their location and the very fact that they still live hidden. Even Jean's psionic link to Cyclops has been severed. Also interesting is the fact that Cyclops' uncontrollable optic blasts seem to be suppressed or contained.

Whatever mission Beast has in mind, he seems to think that he and Cyclops need to finally work together. Has this fallen X-Man regained his moral compass at long last? What is he up to, exactly? We'll have to keep reading MacKay's X-Men series to find out.

For more, check out our exclusive Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles interview with writer Kevin Smith and learn more about DC's Absolute Justice crossover.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.
